hero.title: The colony has many doors. We're mapping them all.
hero.lede: Quién Gana is a public-accountability platform that traces the colonial circuits moving wealth out of Puerto Rico: pension raids, tax havens, disaster contracts, pharmaceutical extraction, energy privatization, real-estate displacement, and the federal debt machinery itself. It connects the people on every end of the wire.

thesis.label: The thesis
thesis.title: Not scandals. A machine.
thesis.p1: Each story you've read about Puerto Rico (the debt crisis, LUMA, the crypto bros, Maria's missing billions, the privatized hospitals, the closed schools) is usually told as its own scandal. As if the actors were unrelated. As if the pattern were coincidence.
thesis.p2: It isn't. It's one machine with many circuits. Federal law builds the channels. Wall Street and corporate America run product through them. The colony pays. The metropole collects. The same firms appear in case after case. The same Congressional moves enable each one.
thesis.p3: Quién Gana documents the machine in public, circuit by circuit, name by name, dollar by dollar. We don't just expose extraction. We connect the wronged to the unwitting to the responsible, so that organizing becomes possible.
thesis.quote: “La colonia paga. Wall Street cobra. El Congreso escribe las reglas para ambos.”

circuits.label: The investigations
circuits.title: Seven circuits. One machine.
circuits.intro: Each circuit is a separate investigation: its own data, its own actors, its own ground-level reality. Together they map the colonial extraction apparatus in motion.

pensiones.mechanism: Vulture funds bought Puerto Rico's retirement-system bonds at pennies on the dollar, then sued in bankruptcy court to take money from retired teachers and firefighters first. Their largest clients? Public pension funds in Oregon, Washington, New York, California, and beyond.
pensiones.statLabel: US public-pension money in vulture funds

coloniaFiscal.mechanism: Crypto bros and hedge funders relocate to Puerto Rico to pay near-zero capital gains and a 4% corporate rate, while displacing locals and contributing little. The beneficiaries are publicly listed at Hacienda. We're making the list useful.

luma.mechanism: LUMA Energy (a consortium of Canada's ATCO and Texas's Quanta Services) took over Puerto Rico's transmission and distribution grid in 2021. Outages got worse. Bills went up. Executive compensation soared. The contract terms remain largely opaque to the public it serves.

laJunta.mechanism: The unelected fiscal control board still holds veto power over Puerto Rico's budget, laws, and labor protections, nearly a decade in. A live dashboard of where each month's tax revenue actually goes: debt service vs. schools, hospitals, infrastructure.

contratos.mechanism: Post-Maria, post-earthquake, post-Fiona: who got the FEMA, HUD, and Army Corps contracts? Whitefish Energy, COBRA, Tetra Tech, and dozens of others moved billions through Puerto Rico while rebuilding stalled. The data is on USASpending. We're making it readable.

farma.mechanism: Look up the drugs you take: see if they're made in Puerto Rico, and which company books the profits there. Pfizer, AbbVie, Lilly, BMS, Amgen, and J&J use Puerto Rican subsidiaries to pay minimal effective rates on US-bound medications.
farma.statLabel: Of top 20 US drugs made in PR

desalojo.mechanism: Rincón, Aguadilla, Old San Juan, Vieques, Culebra. Long-term housing converts to Airbnb. Beachfront privatizes. Renters get pushed inland, or off the island entirely. Block by block, owner by owner, we're mapping who's buying and who's being pushed.

infra.label: The infrastructure
infra.title: The platform connects the investigations.
infra.intro: Each circuit feeds the same infrastructure: a unified map of actors, a wire that surfaces every news mention, tools for divestment campaigns, and an open contribution layer.

mapa.name: El Mapa
mapa.body: Every actor, on the map. Act 60 settlers pinned to their addresses. Disaster contractors at their project sites. Pharma plants in their towns. Pension funds in their state capitals. Geography turns abstraction into territory.

cable.name: El Cable
cable.body: A real-time feed that surfaces every news article mentioning any entity in our databases. Quién Gana becomes the place to track ongoing fights: not a campaign that goes stale, but a living archive that organizers, journalists, and researchers can return to weekly.

herramientas.name: Las Herramientas
herramientas.body: Once you learn your pension is in Oaktree, you need a next step. Pre-written letters to fund trustees. Model resolutions for union locals. A tracker of which funds have divested under pressure. The piece most accountability projects skip, and the one that turns inbound traffic into actual power.

expediente.name: Completar el Expediente
expediente.body: For every entry in every database, anyone can add documentation: photos, news clippings, court filings, personal testimony. Moderated, not free-for-all. Wiki-style depth without surrendering quality. The corpus grows without our team doing every keystroke.

about.label: Who we are
about.title: Boricuas Antifascistas.
about.p1: We are diaspora and on-island Puerto Ricans building public-accountability infrastructure in service of decolonization. We are not a 501(c)3. We are not a think tank. We are not waiting for permission.
about.p2: Quién Gana exists because the colony's extraction machinery is documented in scattered fragments (court filings here, SEC disclosures there, Hacienda registries somewhere else), but the fragments don't talk to each other. The connections only come into focus when someone insists on putting them together. We're insisting.

principles.title: Public record only
principles.body: Every claim sources to documents anyone can verify. We don't smear; we cite.

principles.title: Bilingual by default
principles.body: Spanish and English from day one. The diaspora and the island read the same page.

principles.title: In service, not in front
principles.body: On-island organizers lead. We build tools that serve their fights, not the other way around.

principles.title: Open to contribution
principles.body: Researchers, journalists, organizers, affected families: the platform is yours to extend.

intake.label: Get involved
intake.title: Tell us what you're seeing.
intake.intro: The machine relies on the fact that nobody connects the dots. Pension trustees rely on the fact that their members never look. Act 60 settlers rely on being invisible to their neighbors. We're building a list of people who can change that.
